claim: Let \(R=L(Q_4)\) be the line graph of the four-dimensional hypercube graph, equipped with its shortest-path metric, and let \(K=\mathrm{VR}_{\le 2}(R)\). Then \(\widetilde H_3(K;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z\), \(\widetilde H_5(K;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^8\), and all other reduced integral homology groups vanish. In particular, the scale-two Rips complex of the rectified tesseract has genuinely mixed-dimensional homology and cannot be homotopy equivalent to a wedge of spheres all in one dimension.
integrity: The face enumeration, Hasse-cover acyclicity certificate, critical-cell census, and independent mod-two boundary ranks are replayed from the packaged verifier. No independent external audit is claimed.
scientific_limitations: The computation determines the complete reduced integral homology but not the full homotopy type; in particular it does not determine the attaching maps of the critical 5-cells to the 3-skeleton.
title: Scale-two Rips homology of the rectified tesseract
